items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1810

SPONSOR: SKOUFIS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the town law, in relation to authorizing the town of
Chester, county of Orange to establish community preservation funds; to
amend the tax law, in relation to authorizing the town of Chester to
impose a real estate transfer tax with revenues therefrom to be deposit-
ed in said community preservation fund; and providing for the repeal of
certain provisions upon expiration thereof

 
PURPOSE:

To authorize the town of Chester, in Orange County, to establish commu-
nity preservation funds.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Amends the Town Law by adding a new section 64-k.

Section 2: Amends the Tax Law by adding a new article 31-A-4.

Section 3: contains the severability clause.

Section 4: Effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This legislation would give the Town of Chester the authority to create
Community Preservation Funds to protect its farmland and open space. The
Town of Chester believes this is a major step in preserving its rural
character.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2020 : S8649 Referred to Local Governments / A10759 Referred to Local
Governments

2019/20: S5640B/A7592 2018/19: S8890A/A11186;

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately; provided, however, that section
two of this act shall take effect on the ninetieth day after it shall
have become a law and shall expire December 31, 2040 when upon such date
the provisions of such section shall be deemed repealed.

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 157
 
TO THE SENATE:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:
 
Senate Bill Number 1810-A, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to amend the town law, in relation to authorizing the town
      of Chester, county of Orange to establish  community  preservation
      funds;  to  amend the tax law, in relation to authorizing the town
      of Chester to impose a real  estate  transfer  tax  with  revenues
      therefrom to be deposited in said community preservation fund; and
      providing  for  the  repeal  of certain provisions upon expiration
      thereof"
 
    NOT APPROVED
 
  This bill would permit the town of Chester to  establish  a  community
preservation  fund,  to  be  funded by a new real property transfer tax,
gifts, and other revenues. The stated purpose is to allow  the  town  to
implement a plan for preserving the community's character, including the
preservation of farmland, agricultural land, and other open spaces.
 
  There  has been well-documented tension in the town of Chester between
local officials and members of a  specific  population  of  the  Hasidic
community  which  has also resulted in litigation. Similar unease exists
in the neighboring area of Blooming  Grove.  In  light  of  ongoing  and
historical  tensions, it would be inappropriate to sign this legislation
at this juncture and I am therefore constrained to veto this bill.
 
  The bill is disapproved.                       (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                               __________
